items.headline: London Museum opens its new home on Saturday
items.summary: The former Museum of London opens on 28 November in Smithfield's Victorian General Market after a £437m project, with free permanent galleries.
items.question: The London Museum's new home is in which old London market?
items.explain: It has moved into Smithfield's General Market, opened in 1883 and designed by Sir Horace Jones.

notes.Covent Garden: Covent Garden's fruit, vegetable and flower market moved out in 1974.
notes.Billingsgate: Billingsgate is London's wholesale fish market.

reveal.title: The London Museum's new entrance at Smithfield

items.headline: Thelma Golden to leave the Studio Museum in Harlem
items.summary: After 21 years as director and chief curator of the Studio Museum in Harlem, New York, she will step down once a successor is found.
items.question: Thelma Golden is stepping down after 21 years leading which museum?
options: Studio Museum in Harlem, New York
Whitney Museum of American Art, New York
Museum of Modern Art, New York
items.explain: Golden has led the Studio Museum since 2005; it reopened in a new building in Harlem in November 2025.

notes.Whitney Museum of American Art, New York: Golden worked as a curator at the Whitney earlier in her career.

reveal.title: The Studio Museum in Harlem's new building

items.headline: Venice Biennale visitors pick Nick Cave and India
items.summary: The new Visitors' Lions, voted for by ticket holders after the jury quit, went to the American artist Nick Cave and India's national pavilion.
items.question: Who chose this year's Venice Biennale prizes?
items.explain: After the jury resigned, the Biennale replaced its Golden and Silver Lions with two Visitors' Lions voted for by visitors.

notes.A jury of curators: A jury normally awards the Golden Lions, but this year's jury resigned nine days before the opening.

items.headline: Munch museum in Oslo names a new director
items.summary: Thorsten Sadowsky, who runs the Schloss Gottorf museums in northern Germany, will lead the Munch museum in Oslo from May 2027.
items.question: The Munch museum, which has just named a new director, is in which city?
items.explain: Its 13-storey building on the Oslo waterfront opened in 2021 and holds the works Edvard Munch left to the city in his will.

notes.Bergen: KODE in Bergen also has a major Munch collection, but the Munch museum itself is in Oslo.
notes.Stockholm: Tone Hansen, the museum’s previous director, left this year to run Moderna Museet in Stockholm.

items.headline: Vote looms over I.M. Pei’s Dallas City Hall
items.summary: Campaigners gathered well over the 20,000 signatures needed for a likely May 2027 vote on keeping the 1978 building, which the mayor has suggested the city leave.
items.question: Which British sculptor made the giant three-part work outside Dallas City Hall?
items.explain: Moore’s Vertebra in Three Pieces, also called The Dallas Piece, dates from 1978, the year the building was completed.

notes.Barbara Hepworth: Hepworth’s best-known public work in the United States is Single Form, at the United Nations in New York.
notes.Antony Gormley: Gormley is best known for the Angel of the North in Gateshead.

reveal.title: Henry Moore, Vertebrae, 1968–69 (Israel Museum). The Dallas Piece is a larger version.

items.headline: Van Eyck's portraits reunited in London
items.summary: 'Van Eyck: The Portraits' opened at the National Gallery in London on 21 November and runs until 11 April 2027.
items.question: Whose portraits are on show at the National Gallery in London until April?
items.explain: The first exhibition devoted to Jan van Eyck's portraits, including the gallery's own Arnolfini Portrait.

items.headline: Peggy Guggenheim's London years at the RA
items.summary: Since 21 November the Royal Academy in London has looked at her London gallery, Guggenheim Jeune (1938–39).
items.question: Peggy Guggenheim's London gallery gave the first UK solo show to which artist?
items.explain: Guggenheim Jeune, at 30 Cork Street, hosted Kandinsky's first UK solo exhibition.

items.headline: Hilma af Klint painting sets a Nordic auction record
items.summary: Her 1920 abstract painting Ser III No. 5 sold for 128.9m Swedish kronor (about $12.7m) at Bukowskis in Stockholm on 19 November.
items.question: Which Swedish artist’s 1920 abstract painting just sold for about $12.7m?
items.explain: Hilma af Klint painted it in January 1920, and it made more than 16 times its top estimate; Bukowskis says no artwork has sold for more at auction in the Nordic countries.

notes.Carl Larsson: Larsson is loved for his cosy watercolours of Swedish family life, not abstract paintings.
notes.Anders Zorn: Zorn was a Swedish portrait painter famous for his bathers and society portraits.

items.headline: Venice Biennale closes after a record turnout of nations
items.summary: The 61st Venice Biennale, In Minor Keys, closed on 22 November after drawing 714,015 visitors.
items.question: What record did the 2026 Venice Biennale set?
items.explain: A record 100 countries had their own national exhibitions at this edition.

notes.Longest run ever: It actually ran about three weeks shorter than earlier editions, from 9 May to 22 November.
notes.First edition held outside Venice: This edition was held in Venice, the city that gives the Biennale its name.

reveal.title: The Giardini in Venice, home of the Biennale national pavilions
